title: Pitwall: Faithful Live Commentary via Claim Verification
hook: Live sports commentary has no reference text to check against — facts change every few seconds. This production F1 system verifies every sentence against a live probability model before publishing.
key_points: Live commentary is grounded generation under a deadline: real named athletes, a grounding state that changes every few seconds, no reference text at generation time.
Every published sentence is decomposed into typed factual claims (positions, gaps, tyres, pace, overtakes) and each claim is checked against the probabilistic race state.
The same verifier gates the training data itself: of 3,045 model-written targets, only the 81.9% that are fully state-supported are kept; the rest fall back to a provably faithful template.
Grounding comes from a vectorized Monte Carlo engine (2,000 per-lap continuations), calibrated on 126 races and validated on fully held-out seasons: 90.3% winner-in-top-3 over 155 backtests.
Key finding: virtues trade off and must be gated separately — fine-tuning on richer targets buys vividness that collapses into hallucination when the grounding state is sparse.
content_html: Most faithfulness techniques assume a stable reference document to check claims against. Live sports commentary has no such thing — the facts are about real athletes and change every few seconds. Pitwall, a production system generating Formula 1 strategy briefings in English, Spanish, and Portuguese, treats faithfulness as an architectural property built for exactly that constraint.
extra_html: Every sentence Pitwall publishes gets decomposed into typed factual claims — positions, gaps, tyres, pace, overtakes, race control — and each claim is checked against the probabilistic race state that prompted it. The same verifier gates the fine-tuning data itself: of 3,045 model-written training targets, only the 81.9% whose every claim is state-supported get kept, with the rest falling back to a provably faithful template, so the generator never learns from an ungrounded example in the first place. That verification is only meaningful because the underlying grounding is solid: a vectorized Monte Carlo engine running 2,000 per-lap race continuations, calibrated on 126 races from 2018-2024 and validated on fully held-out 2025-2026 seasons, hitting 90.3% winner-in-top-3 accuracy across 155 backtests. A recurring theme spans both halves of the system: virtues trade off and must be gated separately. Calibration-optimal simulation settings aren't decision-optimal ones; and fine-tuning on richer targets buys more vivid commentary that collapses into hallucination exactly when the grounding state gets sparse — a failure the authors trace to base-model instruction-following, not scale, and fix by auditing for sparse-context cases. The system ran live at two consecutive Grands Prix in 2026, and at Silverstone, a probability trace committed to disk before the race ended had already locked onto the eventual winner ten laps before the flag. Juan S. Santillana, arXiv 2026.

related.title: Why RAG? Grounding LLMs in Your Data
related.hook: An LLM only knows what it was trained on — until it's stale, private, or just wrong. RAG bolts on a search step so the model answers from your data and can cite it.

flashcards.prompt: Why is live sports commentary an especially hard case for grounded generation?
flashcards.back_html: There's no reference text to check against at generation time — the facts (positions, gaps, tyres) concern real named athletes and change every few seconds, unlike typical RAG settings with a stable document to ground against.

flashcards.prompt: How does Pitwall keep its fine-tuning data itself from teaching the model to hallucinate?

choices.text: The same claim-verifier gates the training targets — only the ~82% of model-written targets whose every claim is state-supported are kept, the rest fall back to a template
It manually reviews every training example by hand
It trains on unfiltered data and relies on scale to average out errors
It avoids fine-tuning entirely and uses only prompting

flashcards.explanation_html: Pitwall applies its claim-decomposition verifier to the fine-tuning targets before training, keeping only the 81.9% of 3,045 candidates that are fully grounded — so the generator never even sees an ungrounded example to learn from.
